headline: ‘We are the most famous couple on Instagram’: Meloni tells Modi in France
summary: Italian PM Giorgia Meloni and Indian PM Narendra Modi shared a lighthearted moment during the G7 summit in France, referencing their viral social media popularity.
details: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi met again in France during the G7 summit, continuing their friendly rapport.
During their interaction, Meloni jokingly told Modi, 'We are the most famous couple on Instagram,' referring to the viral nature of their previous meetings and photos.
The two leaders have frequently been seen sharing lighthearted moments at international forums, which often trend on social media platforms.

headline: 5,000 families waterlogged in Gazipur after 3-hour rain
summary: Heavy rainfall has left thousands stranded in Kaliakair, with residents forced to sleep on roads as waist-deep water floods homes and businesses.
details: Three hours of continuous rain caused severe waterlogging in at least six areas of Kaliakair municipality in Gazipur, leaving approximately 5,000 families stranded.
Residents report that roads, businesses, and residential areas were submerged, with some locations experiencing waist-deep water. Many displaced people spent the night on elevated roads for shelter.

Affected areas include Harinhati, Habibpur, Bishwaspara, Rupnagar, Shiyalpara, and the area near Chhapra Mosque in East Chandra. Water remained in many areas more than 24 hours after the rain stopped.
Local residents blame unplanned urbanization, the occupation of canals and reservoirs, and an inadequate drainage system for the frequent flooding during heavy rain.
Some residents specifically claim that constructions at the Safipur Ansar VDP Academy have blocked the water flow under the highway, worsening the long-term waterlogging in surrounding areas.

Kaliakair Municipality Administrator and Upazila Nirbahi Officer H M Fakhrul Hossain stated that canals have exceeded their capacity, slowing drainage. He noted that drain cleaning is underway and efforts to excavate filled-in canals will be taken.
In Ward 5's Dainkini and Hartakitla areas, over a hundred shops, schools, and homes remain submerged. Business owners have suffered losses of lakhs of taka as goods were damaged by the sudden flood.
Health risks have also emerged as contaminated water and waste from dyeing factories have spread into the residential areas.
caption:
5,000 families stranded and waist-deep water in homes. Gazipur's Kaliakair is underwater.

Three hours of continuous rain caused severe waterlogging in at least six areas of Kaliakair municipality in Gazipur, leaving approximately 5,000 families stranded.

Residents report that roads, businesses, and residential areas were submerged, with some locations experiencing waist-deep water. Many displaced people spent the night on elevated roads for shelter.

Affected areas include Harinhati, Habibpur, Bishwaspara, Rupnagar, Shiyalpara, and the area near Chhapra Mosque in East Chandra. Water remained in many areas more than 24 hours after the rain stopped.

Local residents blame unplanned urbanization, the occupation of canals and reservoirs, and an inadequate drainage system for the frequent flooding during heavy rain.

Some residents specifically claim that constructions at the Safipur Ansar VDP Academy have blocked the water flow under the highway, worsening the long-term waterlogging in surrounding areas.

Kaliakair Municipality Administrator and Upazila Nirbahi Officer H M Fakhrul Hossain stated that canals have exceeded their capacity, slowing drainage. He noted that drain cleaning is underway and efforts to excavate filled-in canals will be taken.

In Ward 5's Dainkini and Hartakitla areas, over a hundred shops, schools, and homes remain submerged. Business owners have suffered losses of lakhs of taka as goods were damaged by the sudden flood.

Health risks have also emerged as contaminated water and waste from dyeing factories have spread into the residential areas.
